Where it began

Ollie Pope was born in Chelsea on 2 January 1998. He went to Cranleigh School, which has a family link going back a long way: its first headmaster, Joseph Merriman, was his great-great-great-great-grandfather. He played football and hockey for the school as well as cricket, and turned out for the Guildford and Cranleigh clubs while working through Surrey's age-group sides.

Surrey signed him in August 2016. In the winter of 2017–18 he went to Australia, where he made 994 runs for Campbelltown-Camden in New South Wales Premier Cricket and even earned a commendation in the state parliament for what he did on and off the field.

The player

The year 2018 was his breakout. He made four hundreds and averaged 70.42 as Surrey won the County Championship, was named the PCA Young Player of the Year, and that August made his Test debut against India at Lord's. His first Test hundred, 135 not out, came at Port Elizabeth.

In June 2023 he reached 200 against Ireland at Lord's in only 207 balls, the quickest Test double hundred made in England, beating Ian Botham's 220 balls from 1982. He made 196 in the second innings of a winning Test in India in 2024, and 171 against Zimbabwe at Trent Bridge in 2025. He was named vice-captain in May 2023 and captained England in five Tests, three of them won. By November 2026 he had played 64 Tests and scored 3,732 runs at 34.56, with 9 hundreds and 16 fifties.

What made him special

Good judges, among them Sachin Tendulkar, Brett Lee and Kevin Pietersen, saw a lot of Ian Bell in him: a compact method, a lovely cover drive and a knack for keeping the score moving. He could keep wicket, too, and took 22 Test catches and a stumping with the gloves on top of 57 in the field.

His Test runs did not always arrive in an orderly queue. There were lean spells and there were golden ones, and when he was in the mood he was very hard to bowl at. For Surrey he could be relentless: 812 first-class runs in only nine innings in 2019, at an average of 101, and in 2021 his best first-class score of all, 274 against Glamorgan.

And finally

He was the first Test cricketer whose first eight centuries all came against different opponents. It suggests a batter who liked to share things around fairly, and very few attacks were left out.
